# AWF effort

Use only when durable continuity materially helps. Use `agentic-context`, `agentic-planning`, `agentic-implementing`, and `agentic-reviewing` for their general behavior; this skill owns only AWF effort residency and lifecycle. One user-managed writer updates an effort's memory.

<!-- awf:edit continuity-and-resident: default; create .awf/skills/parts/awf-effort/continuity-and-resident.md to override -->
## Continuity, identity, and resident

Judge continuity at entry and when relevant facts change. Create or resume only when it helps. An effort has a fixed title and slug, one resident with a memory path reported by `./awf effort show <slug>`, and one deterministic managed worktree at `.awf/worktrees/<slug>` on `awf/<slug>`. Do not retitle, create parallel residents or worktrees, infer another topology, or use activity as a lock.

Create with `./awf effort new --slug <slug> "<title>"`. If discussion predates creation, initialize the resident from retained evidence: outcome, settled decisions with actual approval evidence, observations, phase, and next action. Do not reconstruct missing approval evidence. On resume, run `./awf effort show <slug>` to resolve the memory path and revalidate checkpoint claims against repository authority. Memory is a checkpoint, not authority.

<!-- awf:edit execution-and-checkpoints: default; create .awf/skills/parts/awf-effort/execution-and-checkpoints.md to override -->
## Execution, checkpoints, and handoff

Use the exact managed worktree for pre-integration work. Update the reported Markdown memory path with ordinary file tools. Write a checkpoint at a meaningful resumable boundary: completed work, decisions and observations, verification, repository state, next action, and blockers. Before a handoff, leave the effort resumable; the successor uses `agentic-context` to reorient before substantive work.

A changed material outcome needs a fixed-identity successor, not a renamed effort. Create and make the successor resumable, transfer only valid context, then close the obsolete effort safely.

<!-- awf:edit integration-and-recovery: default; create .awf/skills/parts/awf-effort/integration-and-recovery.md to override -->
## Integration, divergence, and recovery

After implementation and any selected review settle, reconcile material deviations in the resident. From the intended clean primary checkout, run `./awf effort integrate <slug>`. Integration is distinct from review, removal, and finish. If it diverges, resolve conflicts visibly, verify the combined result, and obtain renewed risk-based review before removal.

Inspect identity and worktree state before recovery. Preserve unrelated work; do not use blind reset, restore, clean, or stash. Record an intentional recovery and its consequence in the checkpoint.

<!-- awf:edit close: default; create .awf/skills/parts/awf-effort/close.md to override -->
## Close last

When integrated assurance is settled, remove the managed worktree with `./awf effort worktree remove <slug>` without force and verify the path, registration, and branch are absent. Record a reusable lesson where the project keeps durable lessons when warranted. Then run `./awf effort finish <slug>` last. A failed archive move leaves the active resident available for inspection and ordinary retry.
